zh: 每一个操作都会输入 Rogo Intelligence——这家公司的上下文层——将多年的交易经验转化为安全、受治理的机构记忆,使每一笔新交易都比上一笔更强。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So the last time we did this, I think you had 35 million customers, now you have 140 million customers, so well done.
zh: 所以上次我们做这个节目的时候,我想你有 3500 万客户,现在你有 1.4 亿客户,干得好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Busy five years.
zh: 忙碌的五年。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, busy five years.
zh: 是啊,忙碌的五年。

speaker: Unknown
en: One would be tempted to think that with that kind of growth, we've saturated the potential of fintech as a category to
zh: 人们很容易认为,有了这样的增长,我们已经把金融科技作为一个品类创造新平台的潜力——数字化、移动优先之类——挖掘殆尽了,

speaker: Unknown
en: Create a new platform, digital, mobile first, this sort of thing, and that we're maybe in the later innings of the fintech technology transformation.
zh: 我们可能已经处于金融科技技术转型的后期阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know that you think it's the exact opposite, and I'd love you to detail exactly why and what you think we can expect in the next five years, not just for NewBank, but for digital financial services globally.
zh: 我知道你的想法恰恰相反,我很想让你详细说明为什么,以及你认为在接下来五年里我们可以期待什么,不仅是对 NewBank,还有对全球的数字金融服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at global consumer financial services, it's about a $10 trillion industry and still something like 90% of that industry goes through banking branches and is owned by incumbent banks.
zh: 如果你看全球消费金融服务,这是一个大约 10 万亿美元的行业,而这个行业大约仍有 90% 通过银行分支机构进行,并由传统银行所拥有。

speaker: Unknown
en: So while there is a lot of neobanks and fintechs across the world in a number of different areas, we are, all of those fintechs and all these neobanks together, we're less than 10% of that entire market.
zh: 所以虽然世界各地有很多新银行和金融科技公司在许多不同领域,但我们——所有这些金融科技公司和所有这些新银行加在一起——还不到整个市场的 10%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Still in financial services is still almost as if 90% of the world was going to Blockbuster to get VHS and DVDs.
zh: 这就好像金融服务领域仍然是,仿佛世界上 90% 的人都去 Blockbuster 买 VHS 和 DVD。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Netflix-like services still had something like 10% of that industry.
zh: 而 Netflix 类似的服务仍然只占这个行业的 10% 左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that transformation...
zh: 所以那场转型……

speaker: Unknown
en: That migration that you've seen in other industries, in media, with Netflix, in retail, with Amazon, with the Barnes & Nobles, in transportation, with companies like Uber, that migration from incumbents to digitally native companies is still very, very early in financial services.
zh: 你在其他行业看到的那种迁移,在媒体行业是 Netflix,在零售行业是 Amazon 以及 Barnes & Nobles,在交通行业是 Uber 这样的公司——那种从传统企业向数字原生公司的迁移,在金融服务业仍处于非常、非常早期的阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Nubank is very unique, specifically in Brazil and Latin America, because
zh: 我认为 Nubank 非常独特,特别是在巴西和拉丁美洲,因为

speaker: Unknown
en: We are really the only new bank in the world where we've fully surpassed the biggest incumbent bank.
zh: 我们真的是世界上唯一一家已经完全超越最大传统银行的新银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of scale, we now have, in Brazil, close to 120 million customers, so 65% of the Brazilian adult population is a customer of us.
zh: 就规模而言,我们在巴西现在有接近 1.2 亿客户,所以巴西 65% 的成年人口是我们的客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in terms of sheer scale, it's very large.
zh: 所以就纯粹的规模而言,这是非常庞大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even more than that, we become the primary bank account of the entire country.
zh: 但比这更重要的是,我们成为了整个国家的主要银行账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: So about 60% of our customer uses us as their primary bank account.
zh: 所以大约 60% 的客户把我们作为他们的主要银行账户。

speaker: Unknown
en: We replace the incumbent bank.
zh: 我们取代了传统银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not a secondary wallet.
zh: 我们不是次要的钱包。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not some money that you leave that.
zh: 我们不是你闲置在那里的某些钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are the primary institution where people are really banking day to day.
zh: 我们是人们日常真正进行银行业务的主要机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is very unique to Nubank in Brazil.
zh: 而这对 Nubank 在巴西来说是非常独特的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And increasingly, we're doing that also in Mexico and Colombia.
zh: 而且在墨西哥和哥伦比亚,我们也越来越多地做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think that this is a little bit of seeing the future of what will happen around the world over the next 10 to 20 years where you would expect a lot of shift from market share from the still incumbent banks to the digitally native companies.
zh: 我们认为这在某种程度上是在预览未来 10 到 20 年世界各地将会发生的事情,届时你会预期大量市场份额从仍然存在的传统银行转移到数字原生公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is just migration of market share, but also you'll see a significant increase in market size as billions of people across the world entered the banking system.
zh: 而且那只是市场份额的迁移,你还会看到市场规模显著增长,因为全世界数十亿人进入了银行体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: You still have 3 billion people that are completely inside the banking system and don't have access to credit.
zh: 你仍然有 30 亿人完全处于银行体系之外,无法获得信贷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd love to break this into two components.
zh: 我很想把这个分成两个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could imagine if you froze the product today and just worked on getting it in more people's hands, that could be one dimension of expansion.
zh: 你可以想象,如果今天冻结产品,只是致力于把它送到更多人手中,这可以是扩张的一个维度。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then, of course, I'm sure you're thinking carefully about all the wonderful things that AI will allow you to do and technology will allow you to do for customers that you don't yet do today.
zh: 但当然,我相信你也在仔细思考 AI 和技术能让你为客户做而你们今天还没做的所有美好的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you talk through each of those levers to achieve this blockbuster to Netflix transition?
zh: 你能逐一讲讲实现从“大片”到 Netflix 转型的那些杠杆吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The first phase of transformation that enabled a lot of the migration in our industries was the smartphone.
zh: 使我们行业内大量迁移得以实现的第一阶段变革是智能手机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is the same thesis you see repeating through the smartphone is the moment that we get to serve consumers without all that physical infrastructure.
zh: 而这与你在智能手机身上看到的论点是同一个：智能手机是我们能够在没有那些实体基础设施的情况下服务消费者的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have such a gigantic cost structure advantage that we can pass that efficiency to the end customer via lower fees and better product.
zh: 我们拥有如此巨大的成本结构优势，以至于我们可以通过更低的费用和更好的产品把这种效率传递给终端客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to give you a data point, we have 140 million customers with 10,000 employees.
zh: 给你一个数据点：我们有 1.4 亿客户和 1 万名员工。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our competitors have 100 million customers with 100,000 employees and 6,000 branches.
zh: 我们的竞争对手有 1 亿客户、10 万名员工和 6000 个分支机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you start thinking about why the cost of real estate of the branches is gigantic.
zh: 你开始想想，分支机构房地产的成本是多么巨大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our cost to serve a customer is about 3%
zh: 所以我们服务一个客户的成本大约是

speaker: Unknown
en: of what a traditional incumbent bank is.
zh: 传统在位银行的 3%。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means we have so much margin to give back to the customer via no fees, better experience, better interest rates, and overall a better product.
zh: 这意味着我们有大量的利润空间可以回馈给客户——不收手续费、更好的体验、更好的利率，以及整体上更好的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's pre-AI.
zh: 这还是 AI 之前的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're still here in phase one of what a smartphone enabled.
zh: 我们现在仍处于智能手机所开启的第一阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI will be an additional multiplication on that efficiency to that because then you get to choose whether you want to have much more efficiency and you could automatize a lot of areas of the bank.
zh: AI 将是在此效率之上的又一次乘数效应，因为那时你可以选择是否想要更高的效率，你可以把银行的很多领域自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could imagine banks that have 500, a billion customers with 5,000 employees that's within sight, or you can just decide to increase your level of ambition.
zh: 你可以想象拥有 5 亿、10 亿客户却只有 5000 名员工的银行，这在视野之内；或者你也可以决定提高自己的野心水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for somebody like us, especially when we look at
zh: 而对于我们这样的人来说，尤其是当我们看到

speaker: Unknown
en: How early it is in the transformation for us is why don't we go to 100 countries and try to accelerate this transformation by Nubank being one of the leading digital financial services firms in the world.
zh: 这场变革对我们来说还处于多么早期的阶段时——为什么我们不去 100 个国家，尝试通过让 Nubank 成为世界领先的数字金融服务公司之一来加速这场变革呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the craziest things that you can imagine the product or a bank like yours doing for the customer in three or five years because technology has made things possible that weren't before, just like mobile made a lot of new things possible?
zh: 在三五年内，你能想象这样的产品或像你这样的银行为客户做的最疯狂的事情是什么？因为技术让以前不可能的事情成为可能，就像移动技术让很多新事物成为可能一样？

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got a much bigger wave now.
zh: 我们现在面对的是一股大得多的浪潮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, have you really dreamed about what could be possible?
zh: 比如说，你有没有真正梦想过什么是可能的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of those ideas?
zh: 其中一些想法是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We like to categorize the problems that we see in financial services in three buckets.
zh: 我们喜欢把我们在金融服务中看到的问题分为三类。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is access, second is cost, and the third is intelligence.
zh: 第一是可获得性，第二是成本，第三是智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the access side, again, you still have 3 billion people in the world that don't have access to a credit product.
zh: 在可获得性方面，再说一次，世界上仍有 30 亿人无法获得信贷产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's crazy.
zh: 这太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost half of the world does not have access to credit.
zh: 世界上几乎有一半的人无法获得信贷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Even countries like Mexico or Colombia, 13% credit card penetration.
zh: 即使在墨西哥或哥伦比亚这样的国家，信用卡渗透率也只有 13%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why hasn't that happened yet?
zh: 为什么这还没有发生？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you needed the creation of a lot of data.
zh: 因为你需要大量数据的产生。

speaker: Unknown
en: You needed sophistication and credit underwriting.
zh: 你需要成熟复杂的信贷审批。

speaker: Unknown
en: You needed the digitalization of these systems to happen.
zh: 你需要这些系统的数字化先发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is happening.
zh: 而这正在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cash goes away, disappears, enter a number of real-time payment systems, as you've seen in Brazil with PIX or India with UPI.
zh: 现金正在消失、消散，各种实时支付系统涌现，就像你在巴西看到的 PIX 或印度的 UPI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there is a lot of transformation and catalysts that are accelerating the rails on which you increase access to consumer banking for the world.
zh: 所以有很多变革和催化剂正在加速让全世界更多人获得消费银行服务的轨道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is going to be a massive opportunity.
zh: 这将是一个巨大的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: 10, 20 years from now, 100% of the population has access to banking services, 100% of the population has access to credit, 100% of small businesses have access to credit.
zh: 10 年、20 年后，100% 的人口能获得银行服务，100% 的人口能获得信贷，100% 的小企业能获得信贷。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an insane push to global GDP.
zh: 这是对全球 GDP 一次疯狂的推动。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I don't think it's really understood how big of a model this could be for every single economy as you get half of your entire population in some areas access to banking.
zh: 我的意思是，当你在某些地区让你一半以上的人口获得银行服务时，这对每一个经济体来说能成为多大的一个模式，我认为人们还没有真正理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's access side.
zh: 所以这就是可获得性这一面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cost is the one that it tends to be more hidden, especially in developed economies.
zh: 成本则是往往更隐蔽的一面，尤其是在发达经济体中。

speaker: Unknown
en: U.S. is generally a well-served banking services, especially if you're a high-income consumer.
zh: 美国的银行服务总体上是服务良好的，尤其是对高收入消费者而言。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you look at the cost of that banking system, it's pretty significant in ways that are not readily apparent.
zh: 但当你看那个银行体系的成本时，它以一些不那么显而易见的方式显得相当可观。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for example, there's about $15 trillion of retail deposits in the U.S. banking system.
zh: 比如，美国银行体系里大约有 15 万亿美元的零售存款。

speaker: Unknown
en: But banks pay, on average, about 40 basis points on yield a year.
zh: 但银行平均每年支付的收益率约为 40 个基点。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a world where your interest rates are 4.5%, 5%, you look at the calculation of those 15 trillion, that's more or less $600 billion that are going to banks to pay for banking branches that in a digital banking environment would actually stay in consumers' pockets.
zh: 在利率为 4.5%、5% 的世界里，你算一算那 15 万亿的账，大约有 6000 亿美元流向银行，用来支付银行分支机构的费用——而在数字银行环境中，这些钱实际上本可以留在消费者的口袋里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a massive wealth tax, the fact that banks don't pay any yield.
zh: 所以这是一种巨大的财富税，就是银行不支付任何收益率这个事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're high income, you do.
zh: 如果你是高收入者，你能拿到。

speaker: Unknown
en: The lower your income, the less you get paid.
zh: 你的收入越低，你拿到的越少。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a huge tax and that's a huge cost.
zh: 这是一笔巨大的税，也是一笔巨大的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you look at remittances, for example, in the U.S. $100 billion go out of the U.S. People pay 5% to 10% per transaction.
zh: 再看汇款，比如从美国汇出 1000 亿美元，人们每笔交易要支付 5% 到 10%。

speaker: Unknown
en: That will go to zero.
zh: 这会归零。

speaker: Unknown
en: Remittances, moving money, you're moving bits.
zh: 汇款、转账,你移动的是比特。

speaker: Unknown
en: That will trend towards zero in a more competitive environment.
zh: 在一个竞争更激烈的环境中,这会趋向于零。

speaker: Unknown
en: Monthly account, people are paying $5 to $10, $15 per month in the U.S. banking system for a bank account.
zh: 月度账户,在美国银行体系里,人们为银行账户每月支付 5 到 10 美元、15 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you look at Europe or developed economies, Japan, same thing.
zh: 你看欧洲或发达经济体、日本,都一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see a huge amount of cost that consumers are paying that will eventually, with models such as ours that come to compete, will also compete away.
zh: 你会看到消费者支付着巨大的成本,而随着像我们这样的模型加入竞争,这些成本最终也会被竞争掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then finally, intelligence.
zh: 最后是智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is also the one that is less understood and is beginning to be discussed with the advance of intelligence.
zh: 我认为这也是最不被理解的一项,而且随着智能的进步,它开始被讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are in the top 1% of income, you have access to the best financial advice.
zh: 如果你处于收入前 1%,你能获得最好的财务建议。

speaker: Unknown
en: You probably will have a private banker.
zh: 你很可能有一位私人银行家。

speaker: Unknown
en: The private banker is understanding all the bank accounts that you have, is optimizing your deposits, is thinking about what is the right tax efficient structure.
zh: 这位私人银行家了解你所有的银行账户,优化你的存款,思考什么是税收效率最优的结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you need a loan, they're going to go and compete a bunch of different banks with each other and get you the base yield.
zh: 如果你需要贷款,他们会去让一批不同的银行互相竞争,为你拿到基准收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you're in the lower 99%, especially the more you go in the bottom, you have access to nothing.
zh: 但如果你处于另外的 99%,而且越是靠底部,你就什么都得不到。

speaker: Unknown
en: Historically, there's been a lot of conversation about education is the answer.
zh: 历史上,有很多讨论说教育是答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just got to educate people.
zh: 你只需要教育人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: People don't have financial education.
zh: 人们没有财商教育。

speaker: Unknown
en: That never worked.
zh: 那从来没用。

speaker: Unknown
en: People don't sit down to do classes.

zh: 回到 Blockbuster 的类比，我的回答一直是：Blockbuster 拥有海量的数据，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine the amount of people coming in into the Blockbuster and seeing if they were looking at that VHS or that DVD or not or anything.
zh: 想象一下有多少人走进 Blockbuster，看他们是否在看那盘 VHS 或那张 DVD 之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did that data help them build a better search algorithm?
zh: 那些数据有没有帮他们构建更好的搜索算法？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, because they were not capturing the data.
zh: 没有，因为他们没有采集那些数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: They did not have the right systems to capture data.
zh: 他们没有合适的系统来采集数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: They didn't have the right culture, data culture, to be making decisions based on data or based on models.
zh: 他们也没有合适的数据文化，无法基于数据或基于模型来做决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: And somebody like Netflix was able to come in with no data and build a better algorithm and ultimately use that.
zh: 而像 Netflix 这样的人在没有任何数据的情况下进场，构建了更好的算法，并最终加以利用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Scale and data is important, but equally important is your systems and your culture.
zh: 规模和数据很重要，但同样重要的是你的系统和文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: You ultimately be in a culture that is using a lot of this data to make the right decisions.
zh: 你最终要处在一个大量使用这些数据来做正确决策的文化中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this, I think, what differentiates neobanks or more digitally native organizations like us versus the more traditional incumbent banks that are still operating with 15 different systems as a result of a huge amount of acquisitions that they did over the years.
zh: 而这一点，我认为，正是我们这样的新型银行或更数字原生的组织与传统老牌银行的区别所在，后者由于多年来进行了大量的收购，仍在用 15 套不同的系统运转。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they're still, if you look at a lot of the AI applications, I will use AI to transform COBOL.
zh: 而且它们仍然——如果你看很多 AI 应用——我会用 AI 来改造 COBOL。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we get away from the mainframe?
zh: 我们怎么才能摆脱大型机？

speaker: Unknown
en: You're talking about 10, 15 year histories of going to the cloud.
zh: 你说的是上云已经 10 年、15 年的历史了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're still in that process of going and putting systems on the cloud.
zh: 它们仍处在把系统搬上云的过程中。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you run that tactically in the culture to make sure you don't fall in the same trap that like all the big players before you have fallen into, which is that you're suboptimally using your advantages and you don't have a good algorithm?
zh: 你在战术上和文化上如何运作，以确保自己不掉进之前所有大玩家都掉进去的那个陷阱，也就是你在次优地使用你的优势、你没有好的算法？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what is the tactics of you making sure the team doesn't mess that up and actually does the opposite?
zh: 比如，你用什么战术来确保团队不把这件事搞砸，反而真正做到相反？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the biggest difference is that historically traditional banks saw their basis of competition as a lot of banking branches.
zh: 我认为最大的区别在于，传统银行历来把竞争的基础看作大量的银行网点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's literally how consumers used to pick a bank, is I'm going to pick a bank that has a banking branch very close.
zh: 消费者过去就是这么选银行的：我要选一家网点离我很近的银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's why there was a huge amount of effort and energy into real estate and physical infrastructure.
zh: 所以才会在房地产和实体基础设施上投入大量的精力和资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously a lot of focus on building brands and building trust with consumers.
zh: 而且显然大量专注于打造品牌、与消费者建立信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: In financial services especially, you need to protect that trust with consumers.
zh: 尤其在金融服务业，你需要保护与消费者之间的信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's very critical.
zh: 这非常关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we began the company, we did not have to spend energy or focus on an offline world.
zh: 所以当我们创办公司时，我们不必在offline（线下）世界耗费精力或专注。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's more of an online world.
zh: 我们更多是在一个online（线上）世界里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we saw technology and data as a way to build comparative advantage.
zh: 我们把技术和数据视为建立比较优势的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so since the beginning, we saw ourselves as a technology company, not a bank.
zh: 所以从一开始，我们把自己看作一家科技公司，而不是一家银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: A technology company that happens to be in financial services.
zh: 一家恰好身处金融服务业的科技公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And therefore the culture itself has a culture that uses data and analytics consistently for every single decision.
zh: 因此，这种文化本身形成了一种文化，在每一个决策中都持续使用数据和分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what our own foundation model has enabled us is the cost of putting a feature into a model has gone down significantly.
zh: 而我们自己的基础模型带给我们的好处是，把一个功能放进模型的成本已经大幅下降了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pre-AI, you had to spend six months adding a new feature.
zh: 在 AI 之前，你得花六个月来添加一个新功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you wanted to test a new feature in a model, you had to be spending several weeks' work testing this feature, putting it in the model, testing it around.
zh: 如果你想在一个模型里测试一个新功能，你得花好几周的工作来测试这个功能、把它放进模型、反复测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: With our own foundation model, you can test a number of different approaches much faster.
zh: 有了我们自己的基础模型，你可以更快地测试多种不同的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the cost of creating a model, you have an email that has purple letters or yellow letters.
zh: 然后是创建模型的成本，比如你有一封紫色字母或黄色字母的邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: The cost of doing a specific experiment has gone down significantly.
zh: 做一个具体实验的成本已经大幅下降了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so every decision in the organization can now be automatized and be done by model versus a human.
zh: 所以组织中每一个决策现在都可以自动化，由模型而不是人来完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what AI is also enabling.
zh: 这也是 AI 正在带来的改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it kind of let us do what we were already doing at a much more significant scale.
zh: 所以它在某种程度上让我们能够把本来就在做的事情，提升到一个大得多的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the culture itself already existed since we saw this as a way to differentiate ourselves since the very beginning.
zh: 但这种文化本身早就存在了，因为我们从一开始就把这看作是差异化竞争的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think the global financial system will change the most or needs to change the most in the next five years, totally away from your business?
zh: 你认为全球金融体系在未来五年会发生最大的变化、或者最需要变化的地方是什么，完全抛开你的业务不谈?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what are the exogenous changes that you're most carefully watching that you think matter?
zh: 比如说，你正在最仔细地观察哪些你认为重要的外部变化?

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most transformational technologies in the world in France is going to be the first one is the end of cash.
zh: 在法国，世界上最具变革性的技术之一，第一个将是现金的终结。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is happening really everywhere.
zh: 而这确实正在所有地方发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of big cash-heavy economies like Mexico, for example, or Indonesia, or a lot of African countries.
zh: 有很多重度依赖现金的大型经济体，比如墨西哥，或者印度尼西亚，或者很多非洲国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brazil used to be like that, where that cash will go away and will digitalize.
zh: 巴西曾经也是那样，现金将会消失并数字化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mostly through real-time payment systems.
zh: 主要是通过实时支付系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the implications of this, some of them are obvious.
zh: 我认为这件事的影响，有一些是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need banking branches or you need less.
zh: 你不需要银行网点，或者需要得更少了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them are less obvious, which is what happens to the economy, for example, the efficiency of banks when they don't need banking branches.
zh: 有一些不那么明显，比如当银行不再需要网点时，经济会发生什么，银行的效率会怎样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The speed at which money moves in the economy, the amount of data that gets created in an economy that then can be used, for example, to provide access to credit.
zh: 货币在经济体中流动的速度，一个经济体中产生的数据量，这些数据随后可以被用来，比如，提供信贷。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's a big catalyst.
zh: 所以这是一个很大的催化剂。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second one is open finance and open banking across the world.
zh: 第二个是全世界的开放金融和开放银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is basically the concept that you as a consumer own all the data that you have across all institutions.
zh: 这基本上就是这样一个概念：你作为消费者，拥有你在所有机构的所有数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're able to grab that data and share it with anybody else.
zh: 而且你能够获取这些数据并与任何其他人分享。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the biggest sources of inertia in financial services, but also that's called a telecom, for example, or utilities, is that you have a history with a specific company and you cannot transfer that history with somebody else that comes new.
zh: 所以金融服务行业最大的惰性来源之一(电信也是一样，比如，或者公用事业)是，你和一家特定的公司有一段历史，而你无法把那段历史转移给一个新来的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And incumbents have benefited a lot from that inertia of data.
zh: 而在位者从这种数据惰性中获益良多。

speaker: Unknown
en: The moment that you can connect all your history from all your services and pass it to somebody else,
zh: 一旦你能把来自所有服务的历史记录连接起来并传递给其他任何人，

speaker: Unknown
en: You're reducing that inertia and you're enabling more competition for your data.
zh: 你就在降低那种惰性，并且围绕你的数据促成更多竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can monetize that data as a consumer.
zh: 而且作为消费者，你可以把那些数据变现。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can grab your historical information with a bank and offer it to somebody else that is willing to pay for that if you decide to do so.
zh: 你可以拿到你在某家银行的历史信息，把它提供给你决定选择的其他愿意为此付费的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right now, social media does that without you deciding to do that.
zh: 现在社交媒体就是不经你决定就这么做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Increasingly, you're going to be able to do that as a decision.
zh: 越来越多的，你将能够把这件事作为一个决定来做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason why open banking is important is because then it will decrease that inertia globally and will increase significant competition in banking.
zh: 而开放银行之所以重要，是因为它会降低全球范围内的那种惰性，并在银行业带来显著的竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: Banking today globally really is still very much an oligopoly structure.
zh: 今天的全球银行业，实际上仍然非常是一种寡头垄断结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have five, six banks in the US that own 60, 70% of all the assets, same in Europe, same in Asia, same in Latin America.
zh: 在美国有五六家银行拥有 60%、70% 的所有资产，欧洲一样，亚洲一样，拉丁美洲一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that will mean a less concentrated banking industry, much more fragmented, much more competition.
zh: 所以那将意味着一个不那么集中的银行业，更分散得多，竞争多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously that translates into less fees and less cost.
zh: 显然这会转化为更少的费用和更低的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The big trend that has a couple of decades is the role of crypto and stablecoins around the world.
zh: 一个已经持续了几十年的大趋势，是加密货币和稳定币在世界各地扮演的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: What will eventually happen with increasingly people that are much more mobile in nature is that you operate in a combination of the fiat system in your country with a global offshore system.
zh: 随着人们的天性越来越流动，最终会发生的是，你在一个组合中运作：你所在国家的法币体系加上一个全球离岸体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your lives go in between without you even realizing this.
zh: 你的生活在这两者之间穿行，甚至没有意识到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a lot of countries around the world, it's really important.
zh: 对世界上很多国家来说，这非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've seen with the usage of access to Bitcoin, for example, stablecoins, increasingly, they want to bank in the offshore system.
zh: 从比特币的使用、准入上你可以看到，比如稳定币越来越多，他们想在离岸体系中银行开户。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't trust their banking system.
zh: 他们不信任他们的银行体系。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't trust their fiat currency.
zh: 他们不信任他们的法币。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, there's about 190 currencies around the world.
zh: 今天，全世界大约有 190 种货币。

speaker: Unknown
en: My view is that 10, 20 years from now, those 190 will be maybe 10 because the fiscal situation in so many countries around the world is so dire that a lot of that fiat money is not real money.
zh: 我的看法是，10 年、20 年后，那 190 种可能会变成 10 种，因为世界上这么多国家的财政状况如此严峻，以至于很多法币并不是真正的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is basically crypto tokens.
zh: 这基本上就是加密代币。

speaker: Unknown
en: So increasingly, billions of people are going to be banking on the offshore world, U.S. stable coin, but also Bitcoin and other type of assets.
zh: 所以越来越会有数十亿人在离岸世界、美国稳定币上银行开户，还有比特币和其他类型的资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see these two parallel systems interrelating with each other across the world.
zh: 你会看到这两个并行的系统在世界各地相互交织。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you had to think about the US dollar and its importance, if it goes from 190 to 10 or something, do you think the US dollar is the reserve currency 10 years from now?
zh: 如果让你想想美元及其重要性，如果它从 190 跌到 10 或什么数字，你认为 10 年后美元还会是储备货币吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it one of a few?
zh: 还是会是几种储备货币之一？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think its role will be in the world?
zh: 你认为它在世界上会扮演什么角色？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are two sides of that argument.
zh: 这个问题有两面的论点。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can make the case U.S. stablecoins ultimately will be the big savior or one of the biggest saviors of the U.S. dollar because it democratizes access to the U.S. dollar.
zh: 你可以论证美国稳定币最终会是美元的大救星、或者说最大的救星之一，因为它让获取美元的途径民主化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And while the fiscal situation in the U.S. is not great and it's deteriorating fast,
zh: 虽然美国的财政状况并不好，而且在快速恶化，

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still better than the physical situation for the other hundred and plus countries around the world.
zh: 但仍然比世界上其他一百多个国家的状况要好。

speaker: Unknown
en: You look at the balance sheets of all of the central banks or countries in emerging markets in Latin America, it's way scarier.
zh: 你看看所有新兴市场、拉丁美洲那些央行或国家的资产负债表，那要吓人得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you don't have the sovereign capabilities.
zh: 而且它们没有主权能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: At least there is a lot of demand for the US stablecoin.
zh: 至少对美国稳定币有大量需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's very little for the Brazilian stablecoin, unfortunately.
zh: 而对巴西稳定币，很遗憾，几乎没有需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that stablecoin exists for US dollar will ultimately mean that the US dollar maintains its power as a reserve currency for a very long time, but it won't be unique.
zh: 美元稳定币的存在，最终将意味着美元在很长时间内保持其储备货币的地位，但它不会再是独一无二的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you'll have other five, six fiat currencies that people will be saving in and a few crypto tokens where you also be diversifying.
zh: 我认为会有其他五六种法币供人们储蓄，还会有几种加密代币供人们分散配置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've always been a Bitcoin fan and it plays a role in a diversified investment portfolio.
zh: 我一直是比特币的粉丝，它在多元化投资组合中扮演着角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the most surprising thing do you think about the move away from cash?
zh: 你觉得关于摆脱现金这件事，最令人惊讶的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would I not appreciate about the implications of that or how long it would take?
zh: 有什么是关于它的影响或所需时间是我当初没有体会到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what's surprising about going cashless?
zh: 比如，走向无现金化有什么令人惊讶的地方？

speaker: Unknown
en: The main one is what this means for credit markets.
zh: 最主要的是这对信贷市场意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the majority of the world, in the majority of the world economies, still economies are very much offline.
zh: 对世界上大多数地方、大多数经济体来说，经济仍然在很大程度上是线下的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And just think about this situation where you have a taco stand in a corner in Mexico City and you're selling through cash.
zh: 想象一下这样一个情形：在墨西哥城的一个街角有个塔可摊，你是通过现金售卖的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That transaction is not being recorded anywhere.
zh: 那笔交易在任何地方都没有被记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a transaction that you're selling to somebody and it goes away.
zh: 那是你卖东西给某个人的一笔交易，然后就消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that taco stand cannot get credit today.
zh: 而那个塔可摊今天无法获得信贷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, that person has a history where every day they go and sell tacos and they get cash flow that's being recorded, but nobody can underwrite on top of that.
zh: 现在，这个人其实有历史记录——他每天去卖塔可，产生的现金流都有记录——但没有人能据此做授信。

speaker: Unknown
en: The moment that that transaction goes into a digital ledger, that transaction happens digitally, then suddenly that taco seller can take that information to a bank and says, hey, look at my cash flow, give me access to credit.
zh: 一旦那笔交易进入数字账本、以数字方式发生，突然间那个塔可摊主就可以拿着这些信息去银行说：嘿，看看我的现金流，给我信贷额度吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you give me access to credit, I can now have two taco stands or I can have five taco stands.
zh: 如果你们给我信贷，我现在就可以开两家塔可摊，或者开五家塔可摊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Digitalization of the economy and what that enables for credit for a significant percentage of the world population is something that is not very well
zh: 经济的数字化以及它为世界上相当大比例的人口在信贷方面带来的可能，是今天人们还没有充分

speaker: Unknown
en: understood today and is a huge accelerant.
zh: 认识到的东西，而它是一个巨大的加速器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, you look at economies like Brazil, for example, something like 70% of all the employment in the country is still in small businesses.
zh: 再举个例子，你看像巴西这样的经济体，全国大约 70% 的就业仍然在小企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the big corporate, it's small businesses.
zh: 不是那些大公司，而是小企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: The same thing happens in India, for example, or Southeast Asia.
zh: 同样的事情也发生在比如印度或东南亚。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now a lot of these small businesses historically also dealt with cash.
zh: 这些小企业历史上也大多用现金交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now they're digitalizing.
zh: 现在它们在数字化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is trillions of dollars of credit being enabled for billions of people around the world.
zh: 所以这意味着为全世界数十亿人释放数万亿美元的信贷。

speaker: Unknown
en: This could be a significant economic shift for economic mobility across the world.
zh: 这可能是全球范围内经济流动性的一次重大经济转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a very exciting opportunity.
zh: 这是一个非常令人兴奋的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think that you can create creditworthiness versus just predict or measure it once you have all this data?
zh: 你认为一旦拥有了这些数据，你是可以创造信用资质，而不只是预测或衡量它？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, is that one of the goals to like help people become more creditworthy somehow?
zh: 比如说，帮助人们以某种方式变得更有信用资质，这是不是目标之一？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, absolutely.
zh: 是的，绝对是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the first thing you have to do is kind of measure or record a lot of those transactions into a ledger.
zh: 我的意思是，你要做的第一件事就是把很多这样的交易衡量或记录到账本里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what the utilization of cash enables.
zh: 而这正是现金的使用所做不到(所阻碍)的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then with better algorithms and AI plays a role here.

zh: 即使是现有银行也拥有的那种令人难以置信的投资回报率，甚至是在你为提供产品而付出的巨额成本之上，这意味着有一个显著的低价竞争机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who are your biggest influences?
zh: 你最大的影响力来源是谁？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I know you've learned from some of the great entrepreneurs, some of the great investors out there.
zh: 我知道你从一些伟大的企业家、一些伟大的投资人那里学到过东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like when you think about your whole new bank chapter of your life, who are the people that jump out that have most actually influenced how you think about something?
zh: 比如当你想到你人生中全新的银行篇章时，哪些人是真正在影响你思考方式上最突出的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Who are they and why did they influence you the way they did?
zh: 他们是谁？他们为什么以那样的方式影响了你？

speaker: Unknown
en: We began the company as a reaction of a consumer pain, of me realizing how bad consumer banking in Brazil was and how painful it was, and then realizing that this was a proxy for what the majority of the country was actually feeling.
zh: 我们创立公司是对消费者痛点的反应，是我意识到巴西的消费者银行业有多糟糕、有多痛苦，然后意识到这是这个国家大多数人真实感受的一个缩影。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we'll always admire companies that are very consumer obsessed, that know that to win, they need to be able to offer the best product and best service in a way that creates almost fanaticism.
zh: 所以我们一直很钦佩那些极度消费者至上的公司，它们知道要赢得市场，就必须以能几乎制造狂热的方式提供最好的产品和最好的服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so from that perspective, we were very inspired by Amazon.
zh: 从这个角度来看，我们深受亚马逊的启发。

speaker: Unknown
en: Since the very beginning, Amazon being the more traditional consumer obsessed company and how they build this consumer obsession and how they thought about that.
zh: 从最开始，亚马逊就是更传统的痴迷于消费者的公司，以及他们如何建立这种消费者痴迷、他们如何思考这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We studied Disney very carefully because this is a company that wants to create magic experiences.
zh: 我们非常仔细地研究了迪士尼，因为这是一家想要创造魔法体验的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it's not super obvious, but even in banking, a boring banking product, we want to create a magical experience for customers.
zh: 也许这不是特别明显，但即使在银行业，一个无聊的银行产品里，我们也想为客户创造一种魔法般的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: What did you learn from Disney?
zh: 你从迪士尼学到了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's an interesting one.
zh: 这是个有意思的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's the communication that you create with consumers and just simply the magic aspect of it.
zh: 我认为是你与消费者建立的那种沟通，以及它纯粹的魔法属性。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you enter a Disney park, the setup of that entry path that you have, it's almost like you're entering into a kingdom and the service that you get from everybody that works inside Disney and how they treat the young children, spectacles that they create and the fireworks that they create, they're really thinking about how do you create a product that is magical in nature.
zh: 当你进入一个迪士尼乐园时，你所走的入口通道的布置，几乎就像你正在进入一个王国，还有你从迪士尼内部每一位工作人员那里得到的服务、他们对待小孩子的方式、他们创造的奇观和烟火表演，他们真的在思考如何创造一个本质上有魔力的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's something that we push our teams around is for something as boring as sending money
zh: 而这也是我们推动团队去做的事情，对于像寄钱这么无聊的事情

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you create a magic experience out of that?
zh: 你如何从中创造出一种魔法般的体验？

speaker: Unknown
en: The welcome kit that we're sending to our customers here in the US, when they receive that welcome kit of the first credit card, the first debit card, we're trying to create a magical experience in that moment.
zh: 我们寄给美国这里客户的欢迎礼包，当他们收到第一张信用卡、第一张借记卡的欢迎礼包时，我们试图在那个时刻创造一种魔法般的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're very inspired by that.
zh: 我们深受此启发。

speaker: Unknown
en: The customer obsession thing is something that sounds obvious now.
zh: 痴迷于客户这件事，现在听起来是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe Amazon really pioneered this way of thinking.
zh: 也许是亚马逊真正开创了这种思维方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing's for free.
zh: 没有什么是免费的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the trade-offs associated with being so customer-focused?
zh: 如此以客户为中心，其相关的权衡取舍是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's become a popular thing to say.
zh: 说这话已经成了一种流行的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the temptation is like, yeah, everyone's customer-focused to varying degrees.
zh: 而诱惑在于，对，每个人都在不同程度上以客户为中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what does that actually mean?
zh: 但这实际上意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the hard part about being so customer-focused?
zh: 如此以客户为中心，困难的部分是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the hard part is, as with any cultural value, is to do what you say you do.
zh: 大多数公司都会说痴迷于消费者，但当他们突然发现自己因为发明了一项新费用而赚了更多钱时，那么，啊，好吧，也许我在这里不那么痴迷于消费者了，我想多赚一点钱，你就是在把短期置于长期之上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you see it in any company that has very nice sounding values on the wall, then the question is, are they actually executing that, especially when it's inconvenient?
zh: 你在任何一家墙上写着非常好听价值观的公司都能看到这一点，那么问题就是，他们是否真的在执行，尤其是在不方便的时候？

speaker: Unknown
en: Most companies will be consumer obsessed, but then when they are suddenly seeing themselves making more money because they invented a new fee, then, ah, well, maybe I'm less consumer obsessed here and I want to make a little bit more money and you're prioritizing the short term versus the long term.
zh: 大多数公司都会宣称消费者至上，但当他们突然因为发明了一项新费用而发现自己赚了更多钱时，啊，好吧，也许我在这里就没那么消费者至上，我想多赚一点钱，于是你就在优先考虑短期而非长期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually in the entire AI debate, you actually don't hear that much conversation about customers because there is so much energy and focus around how to use AI for efficiency and optimization.
zh: 而实际上在整个 AI 的辩论中，你其实听不到太多关于客户的讨论，因为有太多的精力和焦点集中在如何用 AI 提高效率和优化上。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is much less conversation about consumer obsession here.
zh: 关于消费者痴迷的讨论要少得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is where humans still are building the AI.
zh: 而这正是人类仍然在构建 AI 的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the biggest complexity is actually prioritizing this value, even when it's inconvenient to do so, especially from a financial perspective, but also the AI bro, the tech bro is much more enamored today with the technology versus the consumer experience itself.
zh: 所以最大的复杂性实际上是坚持这种价值观，即使在不方便的时候也要这样做，尤其是从财务角度来看，但今天的 AI 兄弟、科技兄弟也更迷恋技术本身，而不是消费者体验本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really curious how you think about your own product, like literally the thing I see on my phone versus your own agent versus new agents being introduced in the marketplace.
zh: 我真的很好奇你如何看待自己的产品，比如字面意义上我在手机上看到的那个东西，相对于你自己的智能体，相对于市场上新推出的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think there's a world where it actually matters that your marketing is to agents more than it is to humans?
zh: 你认为是否存在这样一个世界，你的营销面向智能体比面向人类更重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, how do you think about that world or whether to provide your own interactive agents versus a product that you're clicking around in on your phone?
zh: 比如，你如何看待那个世界，是提供你自己的交互式智能体，还是提供你在手机上点来点去的产品？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think agents become a customer segment as important as consumers as a segment.
zh: 我认为智能体会成为一个和消费者这个群体同等重要的客户群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you have to provide a product for the agent and you have to market to the agent and you have to do SEO for the agents, right?
zh: 你必须为智能体提供产品，你必须向智能体做营销，你还必须为智能体做 SEO，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the same way we have under a team segment and we have a small business segment.
zh: 就像我们有团队客户群，也有小微企业客户群一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is an entire segment and we're treating it as a segment.
zh: 这是一个完整的细分市场，我们把它当作一个细分市场来对待。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a team dedicated to understanding that segment.
zh: 我们有一个专门的团队来理解这个细分市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: And understanding the needs of that consumer, which is the agent.
zh: 并理解那个消费者的需求，也就是智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that will be equally important, but I don't think it's going to be necessarily 100% of that decision because I think still specifically in banking, and this might be different in other segments, for example, but in banking, you go back to trust and branding and the human will want to know where your life savings are deposited and there is the human aspect of that.
zh: 所以这同样重要，但我不认为它一定会占那个决策的 100%,因为我仍然认为特别是在银行业——这在其他细分市场可能有所不同——但在银行业，回到信任和品牌，人类会想知道你的毕生储蓄存在哪里，这里面有人性的一面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you're still marketing to the human and you're still building the trust with the humans.
zh: 所以你仍然是在向人类做营销，仍然是在与人类建立信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: You got to do both.
zh: 两者你都得做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also for some products, there'll be more delegation.
zh: 而且对于某些产品，会有更多的委托。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for some products, there'll be less delegation.
zh: 对于另一些产品，委托会更少。

speaker: Unknown
en: Specifically for areas like in Brazil, where we have 65% of the entire country as a customer, we have the opportunity to be that agent to the consumer.
zh: 特别是在像巴西这样的地区，我们拥有全国 65% 的人口作为客户，我们有机会成为面向消费者的那个智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the customer is coming directly to our app and asking our agent for support specifically with financial products.
zh: 客户直接来到我们的应用，向我们的智能体寻求支持，特别是金融产品方面的支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we can do it in a way where it's actually an open agent.
zh: 而且我们可以以一种实际上是一个开放式智能体的方式来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It even provides product from third-party banks and third-party financial institutions.
zh: 它甚至提供来自第三方银行和第三方金融机构的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there'll be a mix of this happening at the same time.
zh: 所以这些会同时混合发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I think back to our original conversation five years ago, and you just think about yourself, how you've changed the most in five years, or what surprised you the most in the past five years, what comes to mind?
zh: 如果我回想我们五年前的第一次对话，你就想想你自己，五年里你变化最大的是什么，或者过去五年里最让你惊讶的是什么，你会想到什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: One big change has been this view around five years ago, everybody was working remotely, including us.
zh: 一个很大的变化是围绕五年前的那种看法，当时所有人都在远程办公，包括我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: In order to five years, we've realized how important it is to at least spend some meaningful time in person, in an office.
zh: 到了五年后的现在，我们意识到，至少花一些有意义的时间当面共处、待在办公室里，是多么重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's, I think, a bit counterintuitive, even from what you were five years ago.
zh: 而这，我认为，即使和你五年前相比，也有点违反直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also in a perhaps counterintuitive way, increases the argument to spend time in person more because increasingly the work that AI can do is more or less the work that people at home individually could do.
zh: 同样以一种也许违反直觉的方式，这反而增强了当面共处花时间的理由，因为 AI 能做的工作越来越接近于人们在家 individually 能做的那种工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the individual at home will be competing with AIs and will lose that battle.
zh: 所以在家里的个人将会和 AI 竞争，并且会输掉那场竞争。 [[5019—译注：此处应为 519]] 但围绕协作和身体在场的协调的工作——那正是人类需要做的——才是需要在办公室里发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the work around collaboration and coordination in presence physically, which is what humans need to do, is what needs to be happening inside the office.
zh: 但围绕协作与协调、身体在场的工作——也就是人类需要去做的事——才是需要在办公室里发生的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We went from remote to hybrid and we're spending significantly more time in the office.
zh: 我们从远程转向了混合办公，我们在办公室里花的时间显著增加了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That has been one change.
zh: 这是一个变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the second part is how the organization changes through AI specifically.
zh: 我认为第二部分是组织如何专门通过 AI 发生变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We start paying attention to the technology, but when we tested it, it just didn't really work.
zh: 我们开始关注这项技术，但当我们测试它时，它就是不太管用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just to give an example, we use a lot of Clojure as a programming language.
zh: 举个例子，我们大量使用 Clojure 作为编程语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And through 2025, we kept using a lot of the models for Clojure, for programming specifically, and it wouldn't work.
zh: 整个 2025 年，我们持续用很多模型来专门做 Clojure 编程，但它就是不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was really awful.
zh: 真的非常糟糕。

speaker: Unknown
en: As our most experienced engineers said, this is not going to work.
zh: 正如我们最有经验的工程师所说，这行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we were testing, and Opus 4.6 came in in December of 2025, and that was sort of the moment that a lot of people suddenly realized, no, this actually works.
zh: 所以我们一直在测试，然后 Opus 4.6 在 2025 年 12 月发布，那大概就是很多人突然意识到，不，这东西真的管用了的时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't catch that moment, that switch moment in December.
zh: 我们没有抓住那个时刻，12 月的那个转折时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: We only cashed it 60 days after as a couple of my partners and I were in California and we started meeting with a bunch of early stage entrepreneurs and we said, well, something fundamentally happened.
zh: 我们在 60 天之后才捕捉到它，当时我和我的几位合伙人正在加利福尼亚，我们开始见一批早期创业者，我们说，嗯，某件根本性的事情发生了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we went starting to test a lot of the new models, the new GPT models from Closure and said, holy shit, this is actually working out.
zh: 然后我们开始测试很多新模型，来自 Closure 的新 GPT 模型，然后说，天哪，这真的奏效了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can do Closure very, very well.
zh: 它能把 Closure 做得非常非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It were 60 days where it made a huge amount of difference between us and best-in-class companies that were using AI.
zh: 这 60 天在我们与那些使用 AI 的顶级公司之间造成了巨大的差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we went back to Brazil and we went kind of a cold red around the entire organization.
zh: 于是我们回到巴西，我们在整个组织内进行了一场类似冷启动式的彻底整顿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we took a step back and we're almost in the process of reinventing the entire organization.
zh: 我们退后一步，几乎处于重塑整个组织的过程之中。

speaker: Unknown
en: We mapped out 120 different workflows.
zh: 我们梳理出了 120 个不同的工作流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Across the entire organization, coding is one of them, but everything from how do you do product design, know your customer flows, internal audit, compliance, regulatory capital management, every part of the organization, 120 workflows were reinvented natively using AI tools.
zh: 遍布整个组织，编程是其中之一，但还有从如何做产品设计、了解你的客户(KYC)流程、内部审计、合规、监管资本管理，组织的每一个部分，120 个工作流程都借助 AI 工具原生地被重塑了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had to create a lot of eval infrastructure to be able to measure at every single step how these workflows get reinvented.
zh: 我们不得不创建大量 eval 基础设施，以便在每一步都能衡量这些工作流程是如何被重塑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would say we are more advanced in some, we're less advanced in other ones, but the entire organization is being reinvented.
zh: 我想说，我们在一些方面更先进，在另一些方面没那么先进，但整个组织正在被重塑。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what's so exciting about this moment is we get to reinvent the way we do things with AI technology.
zh: 这就是这个时刻如此令人兴奋的地方——我们可以用 AI 技术重塑我们做事的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And frankly, a lot of the times is that you see huge amount of productivity gains.
zh: 而且坦率地说，很多时候你会看到巨大的生产力提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not even because of AI.
zh: 这甚至不是因为 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's simply there is always opportunity to be reinventing the way you do things actively.
zh: 这仅仅是因为，始终存在主动重塑你做事方式的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we were to do it now without AI, we would find a productivity gains.
zh: 如果我们现在在没有 AI 的情况下去做这件事，我们也会找到生产力提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: But AI just augments the possibility to do that.
zh: 但 AI 只是放大了这样做的可能性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that creates the opportunity, for example, for larger span of control, less manager, much more visibility.
zh: 这就创造了机会，例如，更大的管理幅度、更少的管理者、高得多的可见性。

speaker: Unknown
en: I personally went from having one direct report to 20 direct reports over that period because it just increases your ability to operate horizontally.
zh: 在这段时期里，我个人从只有 1 个直接下属增加到 20 个直接下属，因为它提升了我横向运作的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's less layers on the organization.
zh: 组织的层级更少了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We went from 10 layers to five.
zh: 我们从 10 层减到了 5 层。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the organization went very horizontal.
zh: 所以组织变得非常扁平化。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a bolt of adrenaline to the organization as well in terms of our ability to execute.
zh: 这对组织来说也是一剂肾上腺素,体现在我们的执行能力上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you say more about what made that possible?
zh: 你能多说说是什么让这成为可能的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: So what was happening at One Direct Report and 10 Layers, and then now what's happening at 20 and five?
zh: 也就是,之前是一个直接下属、十个层级,现在变成二十个直接下属、五个层级,发生了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm interested in literally like the day-to-day tactical thing.
zh: 我感兴趣的是字面意义上日常操作层面的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure most CEOs would rather have a flatter, higher bandwidth of information organization.
zh: 我相信大多数 CEO 都更希望拥有一个更扁平、信息带宽更高的组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how does it work?
zh: 那么它是如何运作的?

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what changed in that?
zh: 还有一个心态层面的问题,即你如何真正主动地直接去找那些正在做工作的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is partly AI related, partly is the way we manage our organization.
zh: 我认为这部分与 AI 有关,部分与我们管理组织的方式有关。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for a period of time, as we start scaling significantly and we went from a million customers to 140, the organization just takes a little bit of inertia of itself and it starts adding layers.
zh: 我想有一段时间,当我们开始大规模扩张、从一百万客户增长到 140 时,组织自身就有一定的惯性,它开始增加层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every fast scaling organization goes through the same process because you see things breaking all over the place, right?
zh: 我认为每一个快速扩张的组织都会经历同样的过程,因为你会看到各种东西到处都在出问题,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You have all these growth pains and the easy answer when things are on fire is to just add managers to solve the fire immediately.
zh: 你有各种成长阵痛,而当事情着火时,最简单的答案就是马上增加经理来解决火情。

speaker: Unknown
en: By sort of a natural organic process, we ended up very verticalized and we ended up with a structure that didn't give a lot of visibility.
zh: 通过一种自然的有机过程,我们最终变得非常垂直化,形成了一个没有多少可见性的结构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Partly what AI creates is it allows you to take a step back and reinvent everything about your business.
zh: AI 带来的部分作用是,它让你能够退后一步,重新发明你的业务中的一切。

zh: 一开始当创始人还好,但突然当你看到自己在管理一个非常庞大的组织时,就会想:我是领导这个组织的合适人选吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to, through some thinking and through some experiences and through some feedback, conclude, answer that question for you at some point.
zh: 你必须通过一些思考、一些经历和一些反馈,在某个时刻为你自己解答、回答那个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And answer it definitively on maybe for some reason you're not, but probably you are.
zh: 并且明确地回答它:也许出于某种原因你不是,但很可能你是。

speaker: Unknown
en: That doesn't mean that necessarily the founder will have all the answers and will have all the skills.
zh: 那并不意味着创始人必然拥有所有答案、拥有所有技能。

speaker: Unknown
en: You will need to continue bringing people that add a lot of complementary skills to you.
zh: 你需要持续引入能为你补充大量互补技能的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think at least for me was surpassing that phase of having a voice in the head thinking...
zh: 但我认为,至少对我来说,是跨过了那个脑子里有个声音在想……的阶段

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you the right CEO for the business?
zh: 你是这个业务合适的 CEO 吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: And in making the shape between founder and CEO, because generally you will see founders having both titles, but they're very different functions.
zh: 以及在创始人和 CEO 之间做出区分,因为通常你会看到创始人身兼两个头衔,但它们是非常不同的职能。

speaker: Unknown
en: The founder and the CEO are very different functions.
zh: 创始人和 CEO 是非常不同的职能。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't necessarily fit with each other.
zh: 它们不一定彼此契合。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the key energy of each?
zh: 每个角色的关键能量是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: The founder is impatient, huge amount of sense of urgency.
zh: 创始人是急躁的,有巨大的紧迫感。

speaker: Unknown
en: The founder will want to go run very, very fast, will move fast, extremely fast.
zh: 创始人会想跑得非常非常快,会行动很快,极其快。

speaker: Unknown
en: The CEO will need to be more patient.
zh: CEO 则需要更有耐心。

speaker: Unknown
en: The CEO will need to be more systematic in how it makes decisions.
zh: CEO 需要在做决策时更有系统性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll have to bring generally much more systems thinking into scaling the organization.
zh: 通常要在扩展组织的过程中引入更多的系统性思维。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes those things collude.
zh: 而有时候这些东西会相互冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have to be impatient on one end, you have to be patient on the other end.
zh: 如果你必须在一头急躁，你就必须在另一头耐心。

speaker: Unknown
en: There might be conflicts in that nature.
zh: 这在本质上可能有冲突。

speaker: Unknown
en: Generally, you would think that CEOs are better managers.
zh: 一般来说，你会认为 CEO 是更好的管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Founders don't tend to be good managers.
zh: 创始人往往不是好的管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Founders don't have a lot of patience or willingness to do one-on-ones and sit down and provide coaching to a team.
zh: 创始人往往没有太多耐心或意愿去做一对一、坐下来给团队做辅导。

speaker: Unknown
en: They just want to run.
zh: 他们只想往前跑。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the time, they tend to be much more ICs, individual contributors and managers.
zh: 很多时候，他们往往更像 IC(个人贡献者)而不是管理者。

speaker: Unknown
en: CEOs tend to be better managers because you have to build systems.
zh: CEO 往往是更好的管理者，因为你必须构建系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be thinking more from a system perspective.
zh: 你必须更多地从系统的角度思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the key though for me has been to realize that the CEO title itself and the founder title, you can redesign in different ways too.
zh: 不过我认为，对我的关键在于意识到 CEO 这个头衔本身和创始人这个头衔，你也可以用不同的方式重新设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's being able to do both.
zh: 而且要能两者兼顾。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's being able to have a little bit more patient when you need a little bit more patient, but generally you want to maintain more the founder than the CEO.
zh: 就是当你需要多一点耐心时能多一点耐心，但总体上你想更多地保持创始人的一面而不是 CEO 的一面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's why founder-led companies continue to outperform for decades because if you have to choose, you choose more the founder than the CEO mode, especially in environments where there are big technology shifts, where a lot of the advantages, the assets of the founder come to bear and are more obvious than necessarily the advantages of the CEO.
zh: 我认为这就是为什么创始人领导的公司几十年来持续跑赢，因为如果必须选择，你会更多地选择创始人模式而不是 CEO 模式，尤其是在有重大技术变革的环境里，创始人的优势、资产会发挥作用，而且比 CEO 的优势更明显。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was your lowest confidence moment personally in the entire history of the business?
zh: 在整个企业历史中，你个人信心最低的时刻是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How'd you get through it?
zh: 你是怎么挺过来的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you go through a lot of different phases and I think scaling a business is hard, especially because you're consistently making decisions about situations that you don't really know.
zh: 我认为你会经历很多不同的阶段，我认为扩展一家企业很难，尤其是因为你要不断地在你不真正了解的情况下做决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like for example, I wanted to build a technology company, but I was not an engineer myself.
zh: 比如说，我想建立一家科技公司，但我自己不是工程师。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I needed to go and hire great CTOs and build a great technology organization.
zh: 所以我需要去招聘优秀的 CTO,并建立一个优秀的技术组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did I know how to pick a great CTO at that point if I didn't have the experience or credit, whether it's a lot of specific to financial services and credit expertise?
zh: 在那个时候，如果我没有经验或资历，我怎么能知道如何挑选一个优秀的 CTO 呢，不管这是很多专门针对金融服务和信贷的专业知识？

speaker: Unknown
en: So there was a lot of questioning inside internally, a lot of the decisions that I made about building the team that made me ask myself the question, do we need to bring somebody with more experience from a big bank or from a big organization to run the organization?
zh: 所以我内心有很多质疑，关于我组建团队所做的很多决定，这些决定让我问自己这个问题：我们是否需要从大银行或大组织带来一个更有经验的人来管理这个组织？

speaker: Unknown
en: For a period of time, is this imposter syndrome that is asking you may question is like, are you the right driver of the car as the car becomes more complex and goes faster and faster and faster and faster?
zh: 有一段时间，这是不是冒名顶替综合征在向你提问，就像，当这辆车变得越来越复杂、开得越来越快越来越快的时候，你是不是这辆车的合适司机？

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the most emotional moment in the history of the business for you?
zh: 在企业历史中，对你来说最激动人心的时刻是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Passing a number of different incumbent banks in Brazil was very emotional because for 10 years, all we heard again and again and again, especially from the local experts, was that it was impossible to compete with any bank, that we were going to get crushed, that we were going to die, that these were the most trusted brands in the ecosystem and that we had no shot at being successful.
zh: 在巴西超越多家传统银行是非常激动人心的，因为在 10 年里，我们一次又一次又一次听到的，尤其是来自当地专家的说法是，不可能与任何银行竞争，我们会被碾碎，我们会死掉，这些是生态系统中最受信任的品牌，我们根本没有成功的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: Becoming the largest private bank in the entire country was something incredible.
zh: 成为整个国家最大的私人银行是一件不可思议的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was emotional in terms of what we were able to achieve from a point of scale.
zh: 从规模的角度来看，我们能够取得那样的成就，是很激动人心的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Personally, I was born in Colombia and I had to leave Colombia when I was eight because of all the security situation in Colombia as we grew up and I had to move to Costa Rica.
zh: 就我个人而言，我出生在哥伦比亚，我八岁时因为哥伦比亚当时的安全局势不得不离开哥伦比亚，我搬到了哥斯达黎加。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Colombia was then our country number three.
zh: 而哥伦比亚后来是我们的第三个国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: The moment that I was able to launch Nubank in Colombia, which we did in a big event with the president of the country at the same time, was very emotional as well because there was a bit of coming back home and delivering a product and a service that I thought was going to be very great for the country.
zh: 当我能够在哥伦比亚推出 Nubank 的那一刻——我们是在一个与该国总统同时出席的大型活动上做到的——也非常激动人心，因为那有一点回家的感觉，并且交付了一个我认为对这个国家会非常棒的产品和服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: In an environment where I was being recepted by my people.
zh: 在一个我被自己的人民接纳的环境里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was videocasted and there were 100,000 people connected to the launch of Nubank in Colombia.
zh: 而且那场活动有视频直播，有 10 万人在线观看了 Nubank 在哥伦比亚的发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very emotional too.
zh: 那也非常激动人心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very exciting.
zh: 那非常令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: With all this experience now running the business, how would you define great leadership?
zh: 有了现在经营企业的所有这些经验，你会如何定义卓越的领导力？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm especially interested in the subtle points of what defines, in your opinion, a great leader.
zh: 我对一些微妙的点尤其感兴趣，在你看来是什么定义了一位卓越的领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think first is vision.
zh: 我认为首先是愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be able to see something that few people see, a world that is not as obvious right now.
zh: 你必须能够看到少数人能看到的东西，一个现在并不那么明显未来世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think with the massive information overload that we all live in, it's increasingly harder to have a differentiated point of view about something, about your industry, about your company, about how things are going to move.
zh: 而且我认为，在我们所有人都生活在信息大过载的时代，对某件事——对你的行业、对你的公司、对事情将如何发展——拥有一个差异化的观点越来越难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have to have some kind of vision about the future that is differentiated.
zh: 所以你必须对未来有某种差异化的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you have to be able to sell that vision.
zh: 但之后你必须能够推销那个愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And selling is about inspiring people.
zh: 而推销就是关于激励人们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the time that vision will be very hard or almost feel impossible.
zh: 而且很多时候那个愿景会非常难，或者几乎让人感觉不可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the natural reaction of most people when they are presented with an impossible vision is to push back and to declare it non-realistic, right?
zh: 而大多数人当面对一个不可能的愿景时，自然的反应是推回去，并宣称它不现实，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This phrase, it's not realistic that this is going to happen.
zh: 这句话，这是不现实的，这不会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is not realistic, right?
zh: 什么是不现实的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, look at every single meaningful development in the history of the world.
zh: 我是说，看看世界历史上每一个有意义的发展。

speaker: Unknown
en: At some point, it was defined by somebody to be non-realistic.
zh: 在某个时点，它都曾被某人定义为不现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: The amount of confidence that a lot of the experts or people use when they say it's not realistic.
zh: 很多专家或人们说“这不现实”时所用的那种自信程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be able to sell that vision in a way that a lot of people get motivated by that.
zh: 你必须能够以一种让很多人被激励的方式来推销那个愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: That drives following and motivation.
zh: 那会带来追随和动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But then you have to be able to be a good listener and understand that sometimes you're actually going to be wrong.
zh: 但之后你必须能够做一个好的倾听者，并理解有时候你实际上会是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That vision that you have might not be fully complete.
zh: 你有的那个愿景可能还不完全完整。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is a mode in which you go against the consensus and you completely declare consensus as wrong and you are the complete revolutionary.
zh: 有一种模式是，你对抗共识，完全宣告共识是错的，你是彻底的革命者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nothing about the consensus makes any sense and you will reinvent absolutely everything.
zh: 共识毫无道理可言，你要把一切彻底重新发明一遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is one mode.
zh: 这是一种模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other mode is you're consumed by consensus.
zh: 另一种模式是你被共识吞噬。

speaker: Unknown
en: You think about progress as being unrealistic and things will be the way they are today.
zh: 你认为进步是不现实的，事情会保持今天的模样。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's hard I think about a great leader is you navigate in the middle.
zh: 我认为伟大的领导者难就难在，你要在中间航行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Consensus exists or status quo exists because you think about it from an evolutionary perspective.
zh: 共识存在，或者现状存在，是因为你要从进化的角度去思考它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The vision of the world competed with other visions of the world and it won.
zh: 这个世界的愿景曾与世界上的其他愿景竞争，并且它赢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the world we see today was superior to our possible wars that happened.
zh: 所以我们今天看到的世界，优于那些曾经发生过的各种可能的世界。(原文如此)

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there are elements of that status quo that exist because of a reason.
zh: 所以现状中有一些元素之所以存在，是有原因的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have to be able to understand what are those elements and they will continue to be here.
zh: 所以你必须能够理解那些元素是什么，它们会继续存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also you have to be able to fight that confidential wisdom to see what are the elements will need to be changed.
zh: 但你也必须能够与那种保密智慧(原文如此)抗争，去看清哪些元素需要被改变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think leadership is about knowing what doesn't have to change and pushing to change the things that have to change.
zh: 我认为领导力就是知道什么不必改变，并推动改变那些必须改变的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a combination of conviction, but also active listening and humility to know that you might not have all the answers and that you're going to need to change your mind actively when you do that.
zh: 这是信念的结合，但也是积极倾听和谦逊，去知道你可能没有所有答案，并且当你需要时你会积极地改变自己的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So combining all those different factors, I think is pretty critical for good leadership.
zh: 所以把这些不同的因素结合起来，我认为对好的领导力来说非常关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we think over the next five years for NewBank specifically, I'd love you to paint what you think is like the bear case for the business and the case you worry about and are actively making sure it doesn't happen.
zh: 如果我们想想 NewBank 接下来的五年，我希望你来描绘一下你认为这个业务的悲观情形(bear case)，以及你担心并 actively 确保不会发生的那种情形。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if I think about my rose colored glasses on like the best possible story for NewBank over the next five years, I'd love to hear the two ends of the spectrum from your perspective.
zh: 然后如果我戴上我的玫瑰色眼镜，想象 NewBank 未来五年最好的可能故事，我希望听到从你的视角看这个光谱的两端。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bare case is we are in these three countries in Latin America.
zh: 悲观情形是，我们在这拉丁美洲的这三个国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've saturated them completely.
zh: 我们已经完全饱和了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Growth declines.
zh: 增长下滑。

speaker: Unknown
en: We haven't really been able to find any other growth alternatives from a customer perspective.
zh: 从客户角度，我们真的没能找到任何其他增长替代方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we have 65% of Brazil.
zh: 我是说，我们占了巴西的 65%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Very soon, we're going to run out of Brazilians.
zh: 很快，巴西人就要不够用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ideally, we would see the natality rate in Brazilian current people having more children, but that's not happening.
zh: 理想情况下，我们会看到巴西的出生率上升，现在的人多生孩子，但那没有发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're going to run out of Brazilians.
zh: 所以我们快要把巴西人用完了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We did not succeed in internationalizing.
zh: 我们没有在国际化的道路上取得成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: We ended up being restricted to these three countries and growth saturated.
zh: 我们最终被限制在这三个国家，增长饱和。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the bare case.
zh: 这就是悲观情形。

speaker: Unknown
en: Partly of that would also mean that we could not take advantage of a lot of the AI opportunities that enables also.
zh: 其中一部分也意味着，我们无法利用它所促成的很多 AI 机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's one reason why we're not able to internationalize.
zh: 所以这也是我们无法国际化的一个原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bull case is the opposite of that is we truly took advantage of this thesis that we have around how much market share is going to be transferred from incumbent banks to digitally native companies over the next two to three decades and how that is going to be accelerated by technology shifts like real-time payment systems, open finance and AI.
zh: 乐观情形是它的反面，就是我们真正利用了我们拥有的这个论点，即在未来两到三十年里，有多少市场份额将从传统银行转移到数字原生公司，以及实时支付系统、开放金融(open finance)和 AI 这样的技术变迁将如何加速这一进程。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're able to ride those tailwinds from technology shifts, and we were able to execute through a multi-country platform a global vision of Nubank, taking us to 100 plus countries over the next few decades.
zh: 我们能够乘着这些技术变迁的顺风，并且我们能够通过一个多国平台执行 Nubank 的全球愿景，在接下来的几十年里把我们带到 100 多个国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were able to solve a lot of these big problems that we still think that will be solved.
zh: 而且我们能够解决很多这些我们认为仍将被解决的大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Three billion people don't have access to credit, cash is becoming digital, more people need access to banking.
zh: 三十亿人无法获得信贷，现金正在数字化，更多的人需要获得银行服务。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we have this cost structure advantage versus our competitors, versus the industry players that still own 90% of the $10 trillion profit pool, if we have a cost structure that is 50x theirs, and this is pre-AI, then that meant
zh: 如果我们相比我们的竞争对手、相比仍拥有 10 万亿美元利润池 90% 的行业玩家拥有这种成本结构优势，如果我们有一个是他们 50 倍的成本结构，而这还是在 AI 之前，那就意味着

speaker: Unknown
en: We were able to pass a lot of the efficiency back to the customer via higher yields, lower fees, better experience, fully digitalized, integrating advice in our products, and truly taking advantage of these internationalization opportunities.
zh: 我们能够通过更高的收益率、更低的费用、更好的体验、全面的数字化、把建议整合进我们的产品，把这些效率中的很大一部分返还给客户，并真正抓住这些国际化机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that is the bull case.
zh: 所以这就是乐观情形。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I had you last time, five years ago, I already asked you my traditional closing question, so I have a different one for you today.
zh: 上次见到你时，五年前，我已经问过你我传统的收尾问题，所以今天我给你一个不一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, across NewBank and the incredible experience that you've had building it so far, what is the most interesting lesson that you've learned about entrepreneurship?
zh: 再次围绕 NewBank 以及你至今为止建立它的这段不可思议的经历，你学到的关于创业的最有趣的教训是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How to quickly ignore the imposter syndrome and how the fact that you are the person that had the vision and the energy to build something out of nothing, to give birth, that already is giving you a level of care for that company so high that it will make you become the right leader for a very long time.
zh: 如何快速忽略冒名顶替综合症，以及你是有愿景和精力从无到有去构建某样东西、去将其诞生出来的人，这个事实本身就已经给了你一种对那家公司高到极点的在乎，它会让你在很长时间内成为那个对的领导者。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think anybody in the world cares as much for this company as I do, right?
zh: 我不认为世界上有任何人像我一样在乎这家公司，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: To a level that is almost miserable.
zh: 在乎到几乎痛苦的程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're a father, right?
zh: 你是一个父亲，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have children.
zh: 你有孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nobody will ever care so much about this company, about this company being successful than I will.
